report:
**Conclusion:** 
The claim that prolonged use of cloth or surgical face masks causes dangerous carbon dioxide ($\text{CO}_2$) buildup (hypercapnia) is **false**.

**Summary of Findings:**
Cloth and surgical masks are porous and loose-fitting, allowing air and gas molecules to flow freely. Carbon dioxide molecules are extremely small—far smaller than the weave of cloth or surgical mask materials—and easily escape through the mask fabric and around its edges during exhalation. 

Key evidence includes:
* **Mayo Clinic** confirms that while wearing a mask may alter breathing sensation or feel warm, it does not change the amount of oxygen taken in or carbon dioxide exhaled.
* A study in the **Annals of the American Thoracic Society** evaluated gas exchange during mask use and found no evidence of harmful $\text{CO}_2$ buildup or oxygen restriction, even in individuals with severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).
* **OSHA** (Occupational Safety and Health Administration) addressed workplace safety rumors by clarifying that surgical masks and cloth face coverings do not cause unsafe oxygen loss or hazardous $\text{CO}_2$ accumulation.

While prolonged mask wear can cause mild physical discomfort or feelings of breathing resistance, it does not pose a risk of carbon dioxide toxicity.

**Sources:**
* Mayo Clinic: https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/coronavirus/in-depth/coronavirus-mask/art-20485449?p=1
* Newswise (Annals of the American Thoracic Society study): https://www.newswise.com/coronavirus/face-masks-unlikely-to-cause-over-exposure-to-carbon-dioxide-even-in-patients-with-lung-disease
* Safety News Alert (OSHA Guidance): https://www.safetynewsalert.com/articles/osha-cloth-masks-co2/
* NBC News: https://www.nbcnews.com/health/health-news/mask-myth-debunked-face-coverings-don-t-hurt-lung-function-n1241721
